title: Studio Acquisition Triggers Sublicensing Restriction Dispute
scenario:
**RightsLine — Title: 'Midnight Crossing' (License ID: PRM-LC-2021-0447)**
Licensor: Crestview Studios LLC
Territory: North America (US + Canada)
Rights Window: SVOD exclusive, 36 months from Jan 1, 2022
Sublicensing: 'Not permitted without prior written consent of Licensor. Any transfer, assignment, or sublicense to a third party shall be void unless approved per Section 14.2.'
Status: Active

**FileMaker — Legacy Record (Title ID: FM-8821)**
Title: 'Midnight Crossing'
Licensor: Crestview Pictures (note: entity filed under older trade name)
Deal Memo Reference: GM-2021-CR-003
Amendment Note (added Aug 2023): 'Licensor entity renamed to Crestview Studios LLC per merger filing. No change to deal terms per legal confirmation from R. Okafor.'

**Google Drive — Deal Memo GM-2021-CR-003 (Last Modified: Dec 14, 2021)**
Section 14.2: 'Consent to sublicense shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided that (a) the sublicensee is a wholly-owned subsidiary or affiliate of Licensee, or (b) the sublicensee operates the same streaming platform under a different regional brand.'

**Slack — #content-ops (Mar 3, 2026, 2:47 PM)**
@christopher.adebayo: Heads up — Ridgeline Media closed the Crestview acquisition last Friday. All Crestview titles now roll into Ridgeline's library.
@tanya.moss: Does that affect our sublicensing position on Midnight Crossing? We were about to sublicense the Canadian window to Maple+.
@christopher.adebayo: Checking. The restriction says 'third party' — question is whether Ridgeline stepping into Crestview's shoes changes anything on our side.
@rachel.okafor: The original deal memo has the carve-out for our affiliates. The question is whether THEIR change of control triggers anything.
@tanya.moss: :eyes:
[Thread ends — no further messages]

**NetSuite — Vendor Record**
Vendor: Crestview Studios LLC | Status: Active | Payment remit-to: Ridgeline Media Holdings (updated Mar 1, 2026)
Note: 'Banking details updated per acquisition close. Legal entity unchanged per counsel.'
question: Can Prism sublicense the Canadian SVOD window for 'Midnight Crossing' to Maple+ (an unaffiliated third-party streamer) without obtaining consent from the licensor (now Ridgeline Media)?
choices: A) No — the acquisition constitutes a 'transfer to a third party' under Section 14.2, making the entire license void until Ridgeline re-executes
B) No — Maple+ is neither a wholly-owned subsidiary nor a regional brand variant of Prism, so Section 14.2 requires written consent regardless of the licensor's change of ownership
C) Yes — the acquisition of Crestview by Ridgeline voided the sublicensing restriction because Ridgeline is a 'new' licensor and the original clause no longer applies
D) Yes — the Slack thread shows no objection was raised, which constitutes implicit consent under the original deal terms
rationale: The critical signal is in the Google Drive deal memo (GM-2021-CR-003), which defines the Section 14.2 carve-out. The carve-out only permits sublicensing without consent when the sublicensee is (a) a wholly-owned subsidiary or affiliate of Prism, or (b) operates the same streaming platform under a different regional brand. Maple+ is neither — it is an unaffiliated third-party streamer. Therefore, written consent is required regardless of Crestview's acquisition by Ridgeline. Answer A incorrectly assumes the licensor's change of ownership negates the sublicensing restriction; the NetSuite vendor record confirms the legal entity is unchanged and the license persists. Answer C treats the absence of a reply in Slack as consent, which has no legal basis — 'consent' under Section 14.2 must be 'prior written consent.' Answer D confuses the direction of the restriction: the 'transfer to a third party' clause restricts Prism's sublicensing to third parties, not the licensor's own change of control. The FileMaker amendment confirms entity renaming did not alter deal terms, further supporting continuity.

title: Rights Window Auto-Renewal References Amended Territory in Legacy System Only
scenario:
**RightsLine — Title: 'The Bellwether Tapes' (License ID: PRM-LC-2020-0219)**
Licensor: Arclight Distribution
Territory: 'Per Schedule B'
Rights Type: TVOD + EST non-exclusive
Window: 24 months from Apr 1, 2020, auto-renews for successive 12-month periods unless terminated with 90 days written notice
Schedule B (as entered in RightsLine): 'United States, United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand'
Last Renewal: Auto-renewed Apr 1, 2024
Next Renewal Date: Apr 1, 2025

**FileMaker — Legacy Record (Title ID: FM-6604)**
Title: 'Bellwether Tapes, The'
Deal Modification DM-2022-ARC-001 (entered Jul 15, 2022):
'Schedule B amended per mutual agreement dated Jun 30, 2022. Territory expanded to include: Germany, France, Benelux, Nordics. All other terms unchanged. Amendment executed by VP Content (M. Ishida) and Arclight SVP (D. Kreuger).'
Note: 'RightsLine updated? — TBD (flagged for migration team)'

**Google Workspace — Email thread (Subject: 'RE: Bellwether territory expansion' — Jun 28, 2022)**
From: m.ishida@prismmedia.com
To: d.kreuger@arclightdist.com
CC: christopher.adebayo@prismmedia.com

> On Jun 25, D. Kreuger wrote:
> > Happy to expand into EU territories. One condition: the holdback for Germany
> > must be 6 months from first-run SVOD availability in that market before
> > TVOD/EST can launch. Standard for our EU output deals.
>
> Confirmed. We'll add the 6-month German holdback to the amendment.

Masahiro — looping in Chris for ops tracking. DocuSign went out today.

**Slack — #content-ops (Feb 28, 2025, 11:03 AM)**
@tanya.moss: Chris — 'Bellwether Tapes' auto-renew is coming up Apr 1. Are we renewing? I see it's US/UK/AU/NZ in RightsLine.
@christopher.adebayo: Should be broader than that. Didn't we expand into EU?
@tanya.moss: Nothing in RL shows EU territories.
@christopher.adebayo: Check FileMaker. I think the amendment never migrated.
@tanya.moss: :thumbsup:
[No follow-up message]

**DocuSign — Completed Envelope (Jul 2, 2022)**
Document: 'Amendment to License Agreement — The Bellwether Tapes — Schedule B Territory Expansion'
Signed by: M. Ishida (Prism), D. Kreuger (Arclight)
Status: Completed
Attachment not linked in any other system.
question: If the auto-renewal takes effect on April 1, 2025 without any party sending termination notice, which territories are included in the renewed rights window?
choices: A) Only US, UK, Australia, and New Zealand — the RightsLine record is the system of record and the amendment was never properly migrated

B) US, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France, Benelux, and Nordics, but the German window is subject to a 6-month holdback from first-run SVOD making TVOD/EST unavailable there until the holdback clears

C) US, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France, Benelux, and Nordics — the executed amendment expanded Schedule B and auto-renewal references 'the territory as defined in Schedule B' which was legally amended
D) The renewal is invalid because the territory amendment was signed by M. Ishida (VP Content) who may not have had authority over EU distribution rights post the 2024 org restructure
rationale: The auto-renewal clause renews 'the territory as defined in Schedule B.' Schedule B was legally amended via the DocuSign-executed modification in July 2022, expanding it to include Germany, France, Benelux, and Nordics. The fact that RightsLine was never updated is an operational gap, not a legal one — the executed amendment governs. However, the email thread (buried in the CC chain from 2022) contains a critical constraint: a 6-month holdback for Germany from first-run SVOD before TVOD/EST can launch. This holdback was confirmed by M. Ishida and incorporated into the signed amendment. Answer A incorrectly treats RightsLine as legally authoritative over an executed contract amendment — system-of-record status for operations does not override signed legal documents. Answer B correctly identifies the expanded territory but misses the German holdback condition, which was negotiated in the email and included in the signed amendment. Answer D introduces the 2024 org restructure as a red herring; the amendment was signed in 2022 when Ishida had clear authority, and subsequent org changes do not retroactively void prior approvals.

title: Holdback Conflict Between Legacy Distributor Grant and New DTC Deal
scenario:
**RightsLine — Holdback Agreement (HB-2023-0091)**
Title: 'Dead Frequency' (feature film)
Grantee: Pinnacle Home Entertainment
Holdback Type: EST exclusive, North America
Holdback Window: 6 months from theatrical release date (actual: Sep 15, 2023 — Mar 15, 2024)
Extension Clause: 'If theatrical gross exceeds $15M domestic, holdback extends an additional 3 months.'
Theatrical Gross (per agreement): References Box Office Mojo tracking
Status: Active

**Monday.com — Content Pipeline Board (Card: 'Dead Frequency — DTC Launch')**
Owner: Prism Streaming Team
Planned TVOD Launch: Jan 5, 2024
Planned EST Launch: Feb 1, 2024
Status: 'Ready for launch' (moved to this column Dec 18, 2023)
Comment (Dec 20, @j.navarro): 'Legal cleared this for Jan launch. No conflicts found in RL.'

**Slack — #content-ops (Dec 22, 2023, 9:15 AM)**
@christopher.adebayo: Hey @j.navarro — did you check the Pinnacle holdback on Dead Frequency? It's EST exclusive through March.
@j.navarro: I checked RightsLine. Holdback ends Mar 15 per HB-2023-0091. Our EST launch is Feb 1 — that's inside the window. Pulling it back.
@christopher.adebayo: Wait — did it cross $15M domestic? If so it extends to June.
@j.navarro: Checking...
[Thread continues 2 hours later]
@j.navarro: BOM shows $16.2M. :grimacing: So the holdback runs through Jun 15, 2024?
@christopher.adebayo: Yeah. TVOD should still be fine though — holdback is EST-only.
@j.navarro: :thumbsup: Updating the board. EST pushed to Jul.

**Monday.com — Same Card (updated Dec 22, 2023)**
EST Launch: Changed to 'Jul 1, 2024'
Comment (@j.navarro): 'EST pushed per holdback extension. TVOD Jan 5 still good.'

**Google Drive — Deal Memo (GM-2023-PIN-007, Last Modified: Mar 2023)**
Section 4.1: 'The holdback granted herein was approved by VP Content Operations (M. Ishida) on behalf of Prism Media Group.'
Section 4.3: 'Any modification, waiver, or early termination of this holdback requires approval at the same level or above as the original grant.'

**Slack — #reorg-announcements (Feb 5, 2024)**
@hr.team: Org update effective immediately: Content Operations now reports to Chief Revenue Officer (S. Whitfield). VP Content Ops role eliminated. M. Ishida transitioning to advisory role through Q2.

**Notion — Editorial Calendar (Q3 2024 Planning, last edited May 2026)**
Dead Frequency EST launch: Listed as 'Jul 1, 2024' with note: 'Holdback cleared. Approved by J. Navarro (Sr. Content Coordinator).'
question: Pinnacle Home Entertainment requests an early termination of the holdback in April 2024 (offering to waive exclusivity 2 months early). Who at Prism has the authority to approve this waiver?
choices: A) M. Ishida — he originally approved the holdback and the deal memo requires 'same level or above'; his advisory role preserves his signing authority through Q2
B) J. Navarro (Sr. Content Coordinator) — he has been managing the Dead Frequency release and already made the holdback-related scheduling decision
C) Christopher Adebayo (Content Licensing Manager) — he identified the holdback conflict and has operational ownership of distributor relationships
D) S. Whitfield (Chief Revenue Officer) — as the new leader of Content Operations post-reorg, she holds authority at or above the level of the original approver
rationale: The deal memo (GM-2023-PIN-007, Section 4.3) explicitly requires that any modification or waiver of the holdback be approved 'at the same level or above as the original grant.' The original grant was approved by VP Content Operations (M. Ishida). The Slack #reorg-announcements channel (the critical informal signal) reveals that the VP Content Ops role was eliminated in February 2024 and Content Operations now reports to the CRO (S. Whitfield). Since the role that originally approved no longer exists, the approval authority escalates to the next level in the new structure — the CRO. Answer A is wrong because J. Navarro is a Sr. Content Coordinator, well below VP level; his scheduling decisions do not constitute contract modification authority. Answer C is tempting but incorrect: M. Ishida is in an 'advisory role' — advisory roles do not carry signing authority or decision-making power, regardless of the transitional period. Answer C is wrong because Christopher Adebayo, while operationally involved, holds a Manager-level title which is below the VP threshold required by Section 4.3.
